properties.statement: [BL-195] disconnected_community suggests generate_bridge at a requirement a RULING forbids anyone to satisfy — the detector proposes exactly the forgery the Decision exists to prevent
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Same field report, 2026-08-04.* req:stateless_scaling is reported as a 4-node disconnected cluster. It is disconnected on purpose: a recorded user ruling states that no SATISFIES may be drawn to it, because a requirement backed out of its own implementation is satisfied by construction and can never contradict anything. The suggested fix is generate_bridge \u2014 an agent working the defect list top-down would take it and forge the edge the ruling forbids. The reporter closed the reachability half honestly instead, recording VIOLATES at the named break-point so the hole sits in that component's blast radius; the cluster is still reported, presumably because risk edges are excluded from the structural view \u2014 which is itself worth confirming. This is [BL-179]'s punish-correct-work trap and [BL-176]'s shape from a third direction: declaring the truth in the vocabulary provided does not stop the alarm. Candidate: let an acknowledgement or the governing Decision mark an intended-unsatisfied state, so the detector reports *\"unsatisfied BY RULING (see dec:\u2026)\"* rather than a structural defect with a bridge suggestion. The Decision that governs the unsatisfied-ness is already in the graph; the detector simply cannot see it. Size S", "origin": "Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-195 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: S."}
